summary: Autoscaler metric granularity hysteresis leading to short-lived GPU scarcity in us-west dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday window on 2026-03-10 LuminaAnalytics observed elevated p95/p99 latency for their dedicated routes backed by the us-west reserved pool. The symptom set looked like an intermittent GPU scarcity: short (~30–120s) periods where new attach requests failed or were delayed and throughput across their routes dropped by ~40% causing customer-facing request timeouts.

Impact:
- Customer reported multiple user-facing timeouts and elevated error rates across two critical routes for ML-driven recommendations.
- Observed p99 generator latency increased from ~220ms to 900–1400ms during windows.
- Service degraded for ~18 minutes total across a 3-hour window; impacted business-critical queries.

Timeline / Key events (high-level):
- 12:08 UTC: First alert from Lumina monitoring (elevated p99).
- 12:09 UTC: Support ticket opened and triaged.
- 12:10–12:15 UTC: SRE observed burst of attach failures (attach timeout) in allocator logs for us-west.
- 12:12 UTC: Autoscaler triggered a decision to shrink one overprovisioned slice; shortly after, attach latencies spiked.
- 12:18 UTC: Autoscaler re-expanded but with a ~40s cooldown; intermittent shortages continued until 12:26 UTC.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool: lumina-usw-reserved-1 (multi-GPU A100/NVLink mix).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Routes affected: /v1/generate (high throughput), /v1/chat (medium throughput).
- Models: gptx-13b-int8 (primary), redwood-chat-7b-v2 (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Sustained medium burst of short-lived sessions from customer test cohort (many short streams, 1–3s each).
2) Autoscaler observed drop in moving-average attach utilization (because short streams complete before sustained attach metrics reflect them) and shrunk a slice to reclaim capacity.
3) Immediately after shrink, a cohort of new attach requests arrives; allocator cannot attach into the reduced pool quickly enough -> attach timeouts and delayed batching -> p99 spike.

Observed behaviour & logs (excerpt summary):
- allocator logs (us-west): attach_timeout 2026-03-10T12:11:07Z tenant=lumina route=/v1/generate attempt=3
- autoscaler decision log: shrink slice id=slice-19 reason=util_moving_avg_below_threshold window=60s
- telemetry: moving_avg_attach_util=0.48 at 12:10, instantaneous_attach_rate spike to 2.4x baseline at 12:11
- serving-runtime: increased NVLink stall counters during the shortage windows (nvlink_io_wait++ in 12:11–12:20)

Hypothesis (triage):
- Autoscaler metric window/granularity (60s moving average) causes hysteresis: short-lived bursts drive instantaneous attach demand but do not raise the moving average quickly, triggering inappropriate shrink decisions.
- Shrink operations have a cooldown and require time to re-expand; this combination results in transient GPU scarcity during bursty short-stream workloads (noisy-cohort effect).
- Background snapshotter jobs on a subset of hosts also increased NVMe IO causing attach latency amplification during that window (secondary contributor).

Temporary mitigation / Workaround applied: 
- Support requested emergency temporary override of autoscaler - disabled slice shrink for lumina-usw-reserved-1 for 30 minutes at 12:20 UTC (manual hold).
- Increased autoscaler moving-average window threshold and added a short-term rule to consider instantaneous_attach_rate spikes before shrinks.
- Customer applied client-side retry/backoff (exponential jitter) to reduce immediate fan-in of attaches.

Investigation next steps / planned remediation:
- Engineering to adjust autoscaler heuristic: add fast-path detection for high instantaneous attach rate to prevent shrink while short-burst demand is present (PR referenced below).
- Add a pre-shrink check: if instantaneous_attach_rate > 1.5x baseline in last 15s, block shrink or delay by X seconds.
- Improve telemetry: surface instantaneous_attach_rate and short-stream histograms in Console per-slice.
- Analyze background snapshot schedule on affected hosts and consider staggering to reduce IO coupling with peak attach windows.

Owner / Contacts:
- SRE owner: Daniel Kim (assignee).
- Support liaison: Aisha Patel (reporter).
- Customer contact: Maria Chen (Lumina analytics infra lead) via #support-lumina slack channel and lumina@contacts.lumina.com.

References and crosslinks:
- Slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p167849xxx (internal triage thread)
- Allocator debugger trace: s3://redwood-alloc-traces/us-west/2026-03-10/trace-931999.log
- Related PR (short-term): github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1708
- Runbook consulted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-autoscale-triage

Acceptance criteria for full resolution:
- No producer-initiated shrinks for lumina routes during short-burst patterns without a fast-path check in place.
- Autoscaler changes merged and rolled out to canary and us-west with monitoring dashboards for instantaneous_attach_rate.
- Post-deploy 72-hour observation window showing no recurrence for similar workload pattern.
